_meta.description: Machine-readable crosswalk from EU AI Act articles (the repo's existing control_catalog universe) to ISO/IEC 42001:2023 clauses/Annex A controls and NIST AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1) function-and-category references. This is a MAPPING only — a citation that an article corresponds to a clause/subcategory, with a source and a confidence label. It is not a computed conformity verdict for either ISO/IEC 42001 or NIST AI RMF: only EU_AI_ACT gets a deterministic pass/gap verdict from opencomplai today (see D-3 in PLAN/CLOSE-P1/00-OVERVIEW.md). A smaller initial set focused on the articles packages/core/src/opencomplai_core/control_catalog.py already covers, not exhaustive. Every row is needs_founder_review=true and every confidence is deliberately conservative ('low' unless the mapping is a well-established textbook correspondence) — this is compliance-facing content that has not been confirmed by a human reviewer or legal counsel.

confidence_definitions.medium: A well-established, commonly-cited correspondence between the article's subject matter and the cited clause/category (e.g. Art. 17 quality management <-> ISO/IEC 42001 as a whole).
confidence_definitions.low: A plausible topical correspondence, but the exact clause/sub-clause or subcategory number should be independently verified before being relied on.

sources.iso_42001: ISO/IEC 42001:2023, Information technology — Artificial intelligence — Management system (ISO, published December 2023).
sources.nist_ai_rmf: NIST AI 100-1, Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0), National Institute of Standards and Technology, January 2023.

_meta.not_covered_reason: EU declaration of conformity (Art. 47) and CE marking (Art. 48) are EU product-legislation instruments with no ISO/IEC 42001 or NIST AI RMF equivalent — no row is fabricated for them rather than force a low-value mapping.

rows.notes: AI-literacy obligation topically corresponds to ISO 42001's competence/resourcing clauses; exact NIST subcategory (e.g. GOVERN 2.2) not independently confirmed.

rows.iso_42001_annex_a_control: A.2.2 (Policies for responsible development/use of AI)
rows.notes: Prohibited-practices screening has no direct ISO 42001 analogue; mapped to the organisation's AI policy clause as the nearest governance hook.

rows.iso_42001_clause: Clause 6.1 (Actions to address risks and opportunities)
rows.notes: High-risk classification topically maps to ISO 42001's impact-assessment control and NIST's context-establishment category.

rows.iso_42001_annex_a_control: A.6.1 (Actions to address AI risks in the AI system life cycle)
rows.notes: Well-established correspondence: Art. 9's risk-management-system obligation is the closest EU AI Act analogue to ISO 42001's core risk clauses.
Data and data-governance obligations correspond well to ISO 42001 Annex A.7's dedicated data-for-AI-systems control set.
Technical documentation topically maps to ISO 42001's documented-information clause; exact Annex A sub-control not independently confirmed.
Automatic record-keeping/logging corresponds well to ISO 42001's life-cycle logging control.
Transparency obligations to deployers topically map to ISO 42001's interested-parties information controls.
Human-oversight obligation corresponds well to ISO 42001 Annex A.9's AI-system-oversight-process control.

rows.iso_42001_annex_a_control: A.6.2 (Verification and validation of AI system design/development)
rows.notes: Accuracy/robustness/cybersecurity is a broad article; mapped to ISO 42001's verification-and-validation control as the closest single hook, not exhaustive.
Provider obligations as a whole map loosely to ISO 42001's leadership/internal-organization clauses; this article's obligations are broader than any single ISO clause.

rows.iso_42001_clause: Clauses 4-10 (the AI management system as a whole)
rows.notes: The most direct mapping in this file: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 IS an AI management-system standard, so an implemented AIMS is the natural evidence for Art. 17's quality-management-system obligation.
Distributor conformity obligations map topically to ISO 42001's third-party-relationship controls.
Value-chain responsibilities and substantial-modification tracking map loosely to ISO 42001's change-planning and third-party clauses.
Conformity assessment topically maps to ISO 42001's internal-audit clause, but Art. 43's third-party/notified-body assessment has no ISO 42001 equivalent process.

rows.iso_42001_annex_a_control: A.8.2 (System documentation and information for users)
rows.notes: Transparency obligations for certain AI systems (e.g. chatbots) map topically to ISO 42001's user-information control.
GPAI provider documentation obligations map topically to ISO 42001's technical-documentation control.

rows.iso_42001_clause: Clause 6.1 (Actions to address risks and opportunities)
rows.notes: GPAI systemic-risk obligations map topically to ISO 42001's risk and impact-assessment controls; systemic-risk-specific sub-controls not independently confirmed.
